summary: Gate 1 change summary and Resource Ledger (C++) for 2ef1b9b6c..90364bede (feat/tar-all-sources-default-on; a later origin/dev merge, 81f36f2e4, is not covered). CHANGE: all 16 Echo capture sources ship enabled by default on every OS; the eight formerly opt-in sources (procperf, netqual, module, software, arp, dns, netconn, mapdrive) lose their default_enabled=false initialisers and four init seeds; echo.db schema v7 -> v8 is a one-time SAVEPOINT migration that flips a stored literal false to true for those eight keys and writes <src>_paused_at=0; source_enabled_state() is a tri-state (nullopt = flag unreadable) consumed by every site that ACTS on false (purge guard, process/tcp/module drain-and-discard, boot cursor-source drop, do_configure previous-tcp state) while source_enabled() fails closed; Windows module drain opens each image once through NtCreateFile with OBJ_DONT_REPARSE and takes mtime, trust verdict and signer from that handle; echo.db, -wal, -shm and -journal get a protected owner-only DACL on Windows and 0600 on Unix, a foreign-owned or hard-linked echo.db refuses the open, and app_usage applies the same test through a shared header; server UI strings, docs, changelog fragments and the Echo routed-concern row updated. RESOURCE LEDGER (C++), corrected against HEAD 90364bede (this REPLACES the run-brief text, which was stale for EchoDbDacl and said every exec result was checked before the unwind calls were): (1) echo_db.cpp v8 block: std::lock_guard on db.mu_ for the whole block; SAVEPOINT v8_migration released by RELEASE on success; on failure ROLLBACK TO, RELEASE only if that succeeded, then a plain ROLLBACK if either unwind step failed, all results checked and logged; SqliteErrMsg RAII owner for the sqlite3_exec message; SQL built with std::format from a constexpr key list; no statements, fds, threads or subprocesses. (2) echo_plugin.cpp: no new owned resources; the purge guard holds collect_mu_ (plus software_collect_mu_ for software) across check and delete, lock order collect_mu_ < software_collect_mu_ < EchoDatabase::mu_; the source_enabled_state read for a cursor source now happens BEFORE start(), and RemovableCursorSource has ~RemovableCursorSource() { stop(); }; skip_token() is a pure constexpr function. (3) echo_db.cpp (Windows) EchoDbDacl: the DACL is built from ONE SDDL string, D:P(A;;FA;;;SY)(A;;FA;;;BA)(A;;FA;;;<token-user SID>), through ConvertStringSecurityDescriptorToSecurityDescriptorW; the self-relative security descriptor is owned by sd_, a std::unique_ptr<void, decltype(&::LocalFree)>, and acl_ points INTO it; the SID text from ConvertSidToStringSidW is a LocalFree-owned LocalPtr; the class is non-copyable; there is no AllocateAndInitializeSid, FreeSid or SetEntriesInAclW and no by-value SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR at HEAD. Each file handle in secure_echo_db_files is a HandlePtr (unique_ptr<void, decltype(&::CloseHandle)>); each GetSecurityInfo descriptor is LocalFree-owned. (4) agents/shared/win_echo_db_owner_probe.hpp (new, shared by echo_db.cpp and app_usage open_readonly): class EchoDbOwnerProbe owns the process token with a class-scope HandlePtr alias (the guard closes it even if the TokenUser vector resize throws), the TokenUser buffer in a std::vector<BYTE> (user_sid_ points into it, so the class is non-copyable), the GetSecurityInfo descriptor and the ConvertSidToStringSid string as LocalPtr, and every probed file handle as HandlePtr; owner_allowed is private. (5) echo_module_etw.cpp: ImageHandle = std::unique_ptr<void, ImageHandleCloser> owns the NtCreateFile handle; resolve_ntcreatefile() is a function-local static function pointer (no handle); the UNICODE_STRING buffer points into a std::wstring that outlives the call; WinVerifyTrust VERIFY is paired with CLOSE by TrustStateCloser, a non-copyable RAII struct constructed immediately after VERIFY, so a throwing signer read cannot leak the trust state; drain() wraps the per-event open and sign in try/catch (verdict stays unknown, row kept). (6) quarantine_corrupt_db: std::error_code based file_size/remove/rename (a zero-length sidecar is dropped, a non-empty one renamed beside the quarantine, -journal included); no resource. (7) echo_local_image_path.hpp: pure, no owned resource; the Windows call sites add GetDriveTypeW on a 3-char root (no handle). echo_mapdrive_collector.cpp: constexpr constants and a static_assert; the run_bounded_subprocess call is unchanged. (8) Tests: raw sqlite3 handles are owned by yuzu::test::SqliteHandleOwner; Windows-only cases close handles in small helpers, own descriptors with LocalFree, and aim symlinks and hard links at decoys inside a yuzu_test_ temp dir. There is no manual cleanup left in new C++. The findings of the earlier gate rounds code-review r1/r2 and adversarial-review r1/r2 are not itemised in this fragment; their gate-fix commits are in the branch git log (aba927687, 0ead72b87, 2fb2a4c2a, 46e7b3b3c), as are build-flag r1 (47394b04c), ponytail r1/r2 (b79430593, d213ae45f) and test r1/r2 (54889ac38). summary: FIXED in 1dd7c1f3e (Architect: adopted). The foreign-owner check does not detect a HARDLINK plant: a hard link shares its target owner and security descriptor, so a hard-linked SYSTEM-owned file passes owner_allowed and is then acted on (SetSecurityInfo rewrites the target DACL, WAL initialisation overwrites its first bytes). Exposure is dependent on the data-directory ACL (a standard user needs write-attributes on the target to link it). Fix: nNumberOfLinks > 1 makes a sidecar be deleted and recreated and an echo.db refuse the open, with Windows tests and the phrase "or carrying more than one hard link" in the docs and changelog.

summary: FIXED in 1dd7c1f3e (Architect: adapted; disclosed at the push gate as a tightening of one S4 fail-open branch). The reported mechanism, a sharing violation on CreateFileW skipping the hardening, is REFUTED: the open asks only READ_CONTROL|WRITE_DAC|FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES with full share, so share arbitration cannot refuse it. The same warn-and-continue site hid a REAL bypass: ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED when a planted file withholds WRITE_DAC from the agent skipped the owner gate. Fixed with a READ_CONTROL-only reopen that runs the same owner and link tests. The reviewer graded it LOW.

summary: FIXED in 54889ac38. Agent shard C hit its 240 s TIMEOUT on Windows (baseline 74-108 s) after the one-time mapdrive history backfill queried 5000 logons, a measured 13.1 MB against the 8 MiB output cap, so the capture always tripped output_truncated. The backfill now reads the 500 newest logons with the count pinned to the output cap (shard C 124 s). The shared subprocess runner Windows capture loop is slow in Debug builds (a disclosed follow-up) and Release-build timings were not measured.
